THE BIG STORY
China's growth engine

lines.text: China's economy sped up. Its own shoppers barely did.
lines.say: China's economy sped up. Its own shoppers barely did.

lines.text: China says GDP grew 4.5% from July through September, beating forecasts.
lines.say: China says its economy grew four point five percent from July through September, beating forecasts.

lines.text: That's up from 4.3% in April-June, the weakest in over three years.
lines.say: That's up from four point three percent from April through June, its weakest in over three years.

lines.text: The engine was exports, up 36.3% in September, led by chips and electronics, officials said.
lines.say: The engine was exports, up thirty-six point three percent in September, led by chips and electronics, officials said.

lines.text: But at home, retail sales grew just 1.1%.
lines.say: But at home, retail sales grew just one point one percent.

lines.text: And real estate investment fell 20.6% from January through September.
lines.say: And real estate investment fell twenty point six percent from January through September.

lines.text: Selling far more than it buys pushed China's trade surplus to $938 billion through September.
lines.say: Selling far more than it buys pushed China's trade surplus to nine hundred thirty-eight billion dollars through September.

lines.text: That's on pace for a record, and trading partners like Europe are pushing back.
lines.say: That's on pace for a record, and trading partners like Europe are pushing back.

lines.text: A big growth number can hide a weak shopper, and the world feels it through trade.
lines.say: A big growth number can hide a weak shopper, and the world feels it through trade.

post.ig:
China's economy sped up. Its own shoppers barely did.
China's GDP grew 4.5% in Q3 2026, beating the 4.4% forecast and up from 4.3% in Q2.
Exports jumped 36.3% in September, but retail sales rose just 1.1%.
Real estate investment fell 20.6% in January-September, and the trade surplus hit $938 billion.
Sources: China National Bureau of Statistics and customs data, via Reuters and AP (Oct 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
